arxiv-2402-05119.title: A Closer Look at the Limitations of Instruction Tuning
arxiv-2402-05119.creator: Sreyan Ghosh, Chandra Kiran Reddy Evuru, Sonal Kumar, Ramaneswaran S, Deepali Aneja, Zeyu Jin, Ramani Duraiswami, Dinesh Manocha
arxiv-2402-05119.description: Abstract Instruction Tuning (IT), the process of training large language models (LLMs) using instruction-response pairs, has emerged as the predominant method for transforming base pre-trained LLMs into open-domain conversational agents. While IT has achieved notable success and widespread adoption, its limitations and shortcomings remain underexplored.

arxiv-2403-15959.title: Risk-Calibrated Human-Robot Interaction via Set-Valued Intent Prediction
arxiv-2403-15959.creator: Justin Lidard, Hang Pham, Ariel Bachman, Bryan Boateng, Anirudha Majumdar
arxiv-2403-15959.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Justin Lidard, Hang Pham, Ariel Bachman, Bryan Boateng, Anirudha Majumdar. Tasks where robots must anticipate human intent, such as navigating around a cluttered home or sorting everyday items, are challenging because they exhibit a wide range of valid actions that lead to similar outcomes. Moreover, zero-shot intent-prediction in human-robot cooperative scenarios is an especially challenging problem because it requires the robot to infer and adapt on the fly to a latent human intent, which could vary significantly from human to human.

arxiv-2407-02999.title: Fermi Surface Nesting Driving the RKKY Interaction in the Centrosymmetric Skyrmion Magnet Gd 2 PdSi 3
arxiv-2407-02999.creator: Yuyang Dong, Yosuke Arai, Kenta Kuroda, Masayuki Ochi, Natsumi Tanaka, Yuxuan Wan, Matthew D. Watson, Timur K. Kim, Cephise Cacho, Makoto Hashimoto, Donghui Lu, Yuji Aoki, Tatsuma D. Matsuda, Takeshi Kondo
arxiv-2407-02999.description: Abstract The magnetic skyrmions generated in a centrosymmetric crystal were recently first discovered in Gd 2 PdSi 3 . In light of this, we observe the electronic structure by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and unveil its direct relationship with the magnetism in this compound.

arxiv-2503-11709.title: Conformal Prediction and Human Decision Making
arxiv-2503-11709.creator: Jessica Hullman, Yifan Wu, Dawei Xie, Ziyang Guo, Andrew Gelman
arxiv-2503-11709.description: Abstract Methods to quantify uncertainty in predictions from arbitrary models are in demand in high-stakes domains like medicine and finance. Conformal prediction has emerged as a popular method for producing a set of predictions with specified average coverage, in place of a single prediction and confidence value.

pmc-11640922.title: Metabolomic Hallmarks of Obesity and Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease
pmc-11640922.creator: Diren Beyoğlu, Yury V Popov, Jeffrey R Idle, Łukasz Bułdak
pmc-11640922.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). From a detailed review of 90 experimental and clinical metabolomic investigations of obesity and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), we have developed metabolomic hallmarks for both obesity and MASLD. Obesity studies were conducted in mice, rats, and humans, with consensus biomarker groups in plasma/serum being essential and nonessential amino acids, energy metabolites, gut microbiota metabolites, acylcarnitines and lysophosphatidylcholines (LPC), which formed the basis of the six metabolomic hallmarks of obesity.

pmc-12427087.title: Ketone monoester ingestion preserves working memory during loaded exercise in the heat
pmc-12427087.creator: Blaine S. Lints, Jenica N. Earl, Riccardo F. Romersi, Maria G. Lombardi, Katelynn T. Persaud, Noah K. Nakagawa, Chimaobim E. Martin-Diala, Gianna F. Mastrofini, Adam T. Harrison, Sten O. Stray-Gundersen, James E. Stampley, Shawn M. Arent, FISSN
pmc-12427087.description: BackgroundSpecial Operations Forces (SOF) often operate in extreme heat, where sustained physical exertion may degrade cognition. Exercise-heat stress can reduce cerebral blood flow (CBF) and oxygenation, increasing the risk of catastrophic errors. While ketone monoesters, such as beta-hydroxybutyrate (BHB), may offer neuroprotective effects by improving CBF and energy metabolism, they have yet to be investigated in the context of hyperthermia.

pmc-12452775.title: Decreased Heart Rate Variability Is Associated with Increased Fatigue Across Different Medical Populations: A Systematic Review
pmc-12452775.creator: Sophie Maria Penfold, James Cunningham, Pauline Whelan, Martin G McCabe, John Ainsworth, Jonathan Steven Alexander
pmc-12452775.description: Background: Fatigue has been associated with poorer quality of life and increased morbidity in multiple clinical fields. Patients with autonomic dysfunction have been found to experience poorer physiological health, as well as having an increased risk of comorbidity and all-cause mortality. Heart rate variability (HRV) has been documented as a validated tool to assess autonomic function in clinical practice.

It has garnered considerable attention for its remarkable nutritional and therapeutic potential, deeply rooted in traditional medicine systems [1].

pmc-13348479.title: The RNA-binding protein Pumilio limits polymodal nociception in Drosophila larvae
pmc-13348479.creator: Sara Palega, Hannah Davenport, Rebeccah K. Stewart, Jessica Horton, Andrew Bellemer
pmc-13348479.description: Nociception is the process by which the nervous system detects and processes information about potentially harmful environmental stimuli to generate behavioral and physiological responses. The process of nociception undergoes plasticity in response to injury, inflammation, and infection to shape the sensitivity of nociceptive circuits and the behavioral responses they control.

pmc-13543120.title: MARK4 enhances stress granule formation under oxidative stress and increases tau accumulation
pmc-13543120.creator: Sho Nakajima, Kotone Watanabe, Grigorii Sultanakhmetov, Aoi Fukuchi, Keiya Ito, Sawako Shimizu, Taro Saito, Akiko Asada, Kanae Ando
pmc-13543120.description: Overactivation of Microtubule affinity regulating kinase 4 (MARK4) is believed to contribute to Alzheimer's disease pathogenesis. MARK4 promotes the accumulation of the microtubule‐binding protein tau, thereby enhancing tau‐induced neurodegeneration. However, the underlying mechanisms by which MARK4 enhances tau accumulation are not fully understood.
